_meta: AUTHORED season selectors -- a season only SELECTS over levers that already exist. Design and rules: docs/notes/server_seasons.md. Column meanings: season.gacha_campaign -> the existing gacha campaign key (server/gacha_campaigns.json); season.badges -> the HOME tiles' merqbE18 rows (home_map_button.md), MERGED over default_badges by badge key (a season row overrides the baseline row with the same key); season.home_icons -> the 21-icon strip selection (home_screen_icons.md) recorded for the feature work, not yet server-drivable; season.open.switches -> in-memory switch bits; season.login_month -> the daily-login calendar's month (a key of server/login_calendar.json, e.g. 2019-Jul), DERIVED from the season key when it is YYYY-MM, so it is normally not restated -- an explicit value overrides and "off" leaves the default alone; a season outside the table's 2017-Jan..2022-Jan window falls back to LOGIN_MONTH and logs it (daily_login_bonus.md §7, server_seasons.md §2.3). NEW 2026-09-26: season.default_login_bonus -> the CATCH-UP gift schedules every season inherits, MERGED key-wise by season.login_bonus. total_ladder -> replay the shipped cumulative total-login ladder (F_LOGIN_BONUS_TOTAL_REWARD_MST, 29 tiers, server/catchup_bonus.json); campaign -> the F_LOGIN_BONUS_SP_REWARD_MST group id to replay as this season's login calendar (412 exist, all shipped); welcome -> the AUTHORED fresh-account currency grant (SW-99), the only authored numbers in the facet. Any value "off"/false disables that key. Home: docs/notes/catchup_bonus_family.md.

default_login_bonus._label: The catch-up schedules EVERY season inherits. Nothing here invents content: total_ladder and campaign select SHIPPED tables by id (server/catchup_bonus.json, generated by harness/gen_catchup_bonus.py). The `welcome` amounts are the only AUTHORED numbers in the facet -- retail's real opening gift was server-granted and survives in no artifact we hold (docs/notes/true_new_player_state.md §4), so these are ours, sized to be modest and immediately useful, and must never be quoted as recovered data.

welcome._label: AUTHORED (SW-99). A fresh account's opening currencies, so the economy is not 0/0/0 on day one.

default_events._label: Event facets every season inherits (merged key-wise, like default_badges / default_login_bonus). panel_quest_groups: the PANEL QUEST home icon is ON by construction (its F_FUNCTION_MST gate ships true, so the icon is visible and tappable) but nothing served it, so the tap raised a connection error (SW-121). 10001 is schedule 100 = Rookie Panel Quest (Start your adventure by clearing these quests!), the new-player onboarding panel whose nine quests all have shipped NAMES -- a selection, not content: the rows come from the SHIPPED tables at serve time. Group 1001 is deliberately NOT the default: it is 4-digit and F_TEXT_PANEL_QUEST_NAME has no rows for it, so its titles render as raw MST_PANEL_QUEST_NAME_<id> keys (SW-121). daily_quests: which POOLS today's daily quest is drawn from and how many of them. SELECTION, not content, exactly like panel_quest_groups -- the rows are the shipped text of server/daily_quests.json (the ids ARE the shipped ids, so the client's own MST_DAILY_QUEST_NAME_<id> / _DETAIL_<id> resolve). The floor is in ffbe_config.DAILY_QUEST_DEFAULT_* because the daily quest is reachable by DEFAULT (it is a mode of the SP-challenge list screen, not a gated tile) and a feature that is reachable by default must be served by default -- idiom 39, the panel quest's own lesson. Home: docs/notes/daily_quests.md.

daily_quests._label: The floor: three different kinds of daily quest, one per pool, so the set is three things to do rather than three tiers of one. vortex_gil_summon is first because it is the only pool holding a row whose action a request already attributes exactly (summon <- GachaExeRequest 9fVIioy1).

off.label: no season -- every lever keeps its own default

events._label: THE SEASON-SLOT EXERCISE for the daily quest: the Vortex 'Memories' pool (7000001-7000026, the ids whose shipped names are Collector / Vortex Hero / Raid Hero / Celebrator) replaces the evergreen three. Every id in it is a SHIPPED id with a shipped name AND detail row, so the labels resolve exactly as the default set's do -- which is the whole reason the pools are a selection and not a content switch. The count drops to 2 because this pool's rows are one-per-vault: three would need three vaults and the set is meant to read as a season's flavour.
